title: Dispatch GID 9: Inquiry Ends Public Trials of Concordance Instrument
summary: The voices were real recordings, but the machine’s promised view remains in dispute.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: The Lyceum inquiry has concluded that Dr. Halden’s apparatus permitted contact with a space not present in the building’s plans. It does not certify what any spectator saw there. Their accounts differ too greatly to establish a single landscape, and the Institute warns that the silvered plate appeared to admit observation from either side.

Mabel Crain has returned to work in the Lyceum office but will not enter the auditorium while the plate exists. Her statement describes a crowd whose faces she could not see. She says each person turned toward a different doorway, and she heard their chairs moving whenever the instrument was operated in Alderwick.

Dr. Halden has withdrawn his plans for further demonstrations. Miss Marsh and Dr. Saye have sealed the plate behind an opaque shutter in an Institute vault. Halden maintains that the shared voice showed a true connection between the audience and the Stratum. “It worked,” he said at the inquiry. “That is why it had to be closed.”

Inspector Voss found no new passages in the Lyceum. The two unsold seats have been removed. On the last night of the inspection, a caretaker heard a single chair scrape after the doors were locked; the sound did not recur when officers returned.

Ruth Crain has kept the handbell. She rang it once for our reporter, and Mabel answered from the next room. Neither sister calls the warning a message from the future. Mabel said only that she heard her own voice before she had opened her mouth, and knew she must find the people who could still hear it.
